title: Vertically opposite angles are equal
competencyName: Use linear pairs, vertically opposite, complementary and supplementary angles
familyTitle: Angles where two straight lines cross
skill: At two crossing lines: vertically opposite angles are equal; adjacent angles make 180°; all four make 360°.

knowledge: angles on a straight line add to 180°

concept: Where two straight lines cross, angles next to each other lie on a straight line, so they add to 180°.
Go round: x, then 180° − x, then 180° − (180° − x) = x again. So opposite angles are equal, and all four add to 360°.

alternativeExplanation.title: Two crossed pencils
text: Hold two straight pencils crossed like an X.
Open them wider: the top and bottom angles grow together while the two side angles shrink together. Opposite angles stay equal.

misconceptions.note: vertically opposite taken as a linear pair

whatWentWrong: In "Two straight lines cross each other, making four angles. One of the angles is 104°. What is the angle opposite it (vertically opposite), in degrees?", one wrong answer is 76.
Vertically opposite angles were taken as a pair on a straight line. They are not on one straight line together; they are equal.
Opposite angles do not lie together on one straight line, so they need not add to 180°: they are equal. Angles next to each other make 180°.
screens.counterCheck: Counter-check: going round the crossing, each angle makes 180° with the next one: 104°, then 76°, then 104° again. The angle opposite 104° is the third one round, so it is 104°, not 76°.
solvedCorrectly: the one after = 180° − 76° = 104° (straight line): the opposite angle is 104°

misconceptions.status: modelled (a single matching answer is a SUSPECTED error; established only under misconception-evidence@1: two matching answers)

whatWentWrong: In "Two straight lines cross each other, making four angles. One of the angles is 147°. What is an angle next to it (they form a straight line together), in degrees?", one wrong answer is 147.
Angles next to each other are not equal (unless both are 90°); together they make a straight line, 180°.
Angles next to each other lie on a straight line: they add to 180°. They are equal only when both are 90°.
screens.counterCheck: Check: the two angles together fill one side of a straight line, which is 180°. 147° + 147° = 294° is more than a straight line.
solvedCorrectly: adjacent angles lie on a straight line: 180° − 147° = 33°
